content.text: Carmen, rescued from a convent by Sister Katie and Father Waite, is taken to police headquarters and reunited with Reed and Harris. She attends Elwin Select School, but her unconventional Christian Science beliefs lead to expulsion. Mrs. Hawley-Crowles brings her into New York society, using her beauty, mine ownership, and “Inca princess” identity to gain status. Carmen befriends the Beaubien, an influential financier’s companion, while corrupt businessmen exploit her mine through the Simiti Development Company. At a charity ball, Carmen gives her pearls to a starving woman and challenges J. Wilton Ames’s materialism. She later meets Father Waite at his church and rejects Monsignor Lafelle’s attempt to recruit her into the Catholic Church. The novel contrasts Carmen’s spirituality and love with greed, social ambition, religious manipulation, and financial corruption.
